label: PF Backlog 582
title: Eventing SSOT: Python thin-client cutover of core/events.py over the A1 wire seam (edit-only)
body:
## Problem / why
PY emitters currently write the stream directly; the Go core will own emit/seq. Must cut over with zero
consumer changes.

## Goal / value
core/events.py (edit-only, no new module) delegates emit to the Go core via core/go_host while keeping its
public API and envelope back-compat; reads remain compatible.

## In scope
- Edit core/events.py + core/contracts seam; keep TYPES/EVENT_VERSION/emit/read/counts signatures.
- Feature-flag/strangler: fall back to existing writer if Go host unavailable (fail-safe, not fail-open).

## Out of scope
- New Python modules; changing emit signatures.

## Acceptance criteria
- All 50 events consumers unchanged; test_api_events + test_event_ssot green; no duplicate store.

## Verification / test plan
- Contract test pins public symbols; run event/test suite + precheck.

## Dependencies & links
- E2, E3.

acceptance_criteria: AC-1: core/events.py:emit() delegates event append to go_host.event_append() and populates the monotonic sequence number seq returned by the Go core.

AC-3: Existing public signatures and constants (TYPES, EVENT_VERSION, path(), read(), counts()) remain completely backward compatible.
AC-4: All existing event consumers and test suites (test_api_events.py, test_event_ssot.py, test_event_core.py) pass cleanly.
AC-5: Dedicated contract tests verify monotonic seq assignment and seamless Go-to-Python envelope parity without creating duplicate event files.

existing_path: Python event emitter: core/events.py:43 (emit function appending directly to JSONL).
Go host bridge: core/go_host.py:86 (event_append and event_read wrappers over A1 wire contract).

Fail-safe fallback to direct JSONL append is triggered if go_host returns ok=False or is unbuilt.
divergences: None. Edit-only cutover strictly aligned with BI-PF-1272 specification and store-registry rules.

functional_spec.outcome: Python emitters delegate event emission to the Go core over the A1 wire seam with zero consumer disruption, gaining monotonic sequence numbers and Go event authority.
actors: Python Emitters: Existing pipeline runners, stages, workers, and tasks calling core.events.emit().
Go Event Core: The authoritative append-only store in go/pfcore managing monotonic sequencing.
go_host Bridge: The A1 wire contract interface in core/go_host.py invoking pfcore-host.
scope: core/events.py: Edit-only update to emit() delegating to go_host.event_append with fallback.
non_goals: Creating new Python modules or public abstractions.
Modifying existing caller signatures or removing backwards-compatible envelope fields.
Altering downstream subscriber transport or notification logic (handled in subsequent items).
assumptions: go/pfcore-host binary is compiled or built on-demand by go_host._ensure_binary().
go_host.event_append() assigns monotonic sequence numbers and writes JSON lines under lock.
domain: A1 Wire Seam: JSON-over-stdin/stdout IPC contract between Python runtime and Go native core.
Monotonic Sequence (seq): Strictly increasing integer assigned to each event by the Go authority.
Strangler Pattern: Fail-safe mechanism falling back to local Python JSONL append if Go is unreachable.
